title: Nonstationary arrival-rate scan (notes & quick analysis)
content:
Context / WHY: Quick scratchpad for reproducible runs exploring nonstationary arrivals (time-varying lambda(t)) and how the runtime's batching + cache interact with sinusoidal/step changes. Goal: capture phase-dependent tail behavior, find operating regions where batching helps vs hurts, and identify simple guardrails for routing/pacing.

High-level hypothesis (notes-to-self):
- Slow sinusoidal variations (period > 60s) allow the batching logic to adapt; tail stays bounded.
- Fast swings (period <= 10s) create repeated microbursts that trigger cold-path spikes and increase p99 significantly.
- Mixed patterns (base Poisson + random bursts) reveal path-dependent hysteresis in KV cache hit rates and batch-formation latency.

Quick experimental design:
- Driver: internal bench-runner (single-node client) with deterministic seeds.
- Model: open-llm-13B-quant (fp16-ish, eager KV cache), sequence length: prompt 80 + gen 100 tokens.
- Serving config: batching window 10ms (default), adaptive_burst_coalesce=true, kv_cache_enabled=true.
- Hardware: single vGPU (A100) on dev cluster; same node across runs.
- Measurement interval: collect per-1s histograms of latency (p50/p90/p95/p99) + qps + batch_size_avg + kv_hit_rate.

Arrival processes generated:
1) slow-sine: lambda(t) = 50 + 40 * sin(2*pi*t/120)  (period 120s, QPS approx 10..90)
2) fast-sine: lambda(t) = 50 + 40 * sin(2*pi*t/8)    (period 8s, same amplitude)
3) step-train: alternating 30s@20QPS / 30s@80QPS for 20 minutes
4) base+microbursts: base 40 QPS + Poisson microbursts: bursts of 200 QPS for 2s with p=0.02 each second

Repro steps (commands):
- bench-runner --pattern sine --period 120 --amp 40 --base 50 --seed 20251015 --out /tmp/run_slow_sine.log
- bench-runner --pattern sine --period 8 --amp 40 --base 50 --seed 20251016 --out /tmp/run_fast_sine.log
- bench-runner --pattern step --high 80 --low 20 --dwell 30 --cycles 20 --seed 20251017 --out /tmp/run_step.log
- bench-runner --pattern sporadic --base 40 --burst-qps 200 --burst-dur 2 --burst-prob 0.02 --seed 20251018 --out /tmp/run_burst.log

Key single-run observations (extracted from quick parsing script):
- slow-sine (period 120s, 40 amp) 
  - mean qps observed: 52.3, batch_size_avg: 6.9, kv_hit_rate: 0.78
  - latency p50/p95/p99 (ms): 46 / 79 / 135
  - commentary: latency tracks QPS smoothly; no catastrophic p99 spikes when rate climbs — batching absorbs load.

- fast-sine (period 8s)
  - mean qps observed: 49.7, batch_size_avg: 3.1, kv_hit_rate: 0.54
  - latency p50/p95/p99 (ms): 52 / 130 / 480
  - commentary: p99s have repeated spikes aligned with fast rising edge; average batch size drops (can't form large batches during rapid swings) and KV hit rate suffers (working set churn).

- step-train (30s low / 30s high)
  - oscillation amplitude clear: during high windows batch_size_avg=8.2, kv_hit_rate=0.84, p99~160ms; during low windows batch_size_avg=2.4, kv_hit_rate=0.57, p99~210ms (interesting: p99 higher during low windows sometimes because cold-path activations and slower batching cause queueing), overall mean p99~185ms
  - commentary: abrupt step transitions create transient region where latency overshoots SLO even when steady-state would be fine. Need explicit guardrail: on transition to low, allow fast shrink of concurrency or reduce batching window to drain.

- base+microbursts
  - mean qps observed: 46.8, observed burst peaks near 220 QPS during microburst; batch_size_avg overall 4.0, kv_hit_rate 0.61
  - latency p50/p95/p99 (ms): 47 / 140 / 510
  - commentary: rare high-amplitude microbursts cause very large p99 spikes (500ms+). While rare, they break SLO. Consider soft-priority lanes or short-circuit on microburst detection.

Mini phase-plane (qualitative): each point is a short 10s window labeled by (qps, p99) -> shows a loop for sine. ASCII sketch (slow-sine vs fast-sine):

Slow-sine (phase points):
  low(10QPS)  -> p99  ~ 70ms  [.]
  mid-rise     -> p99  ~ 90ms  [..]
  high(90QPS) -> p99  ~ 140ms [....]
  mid-fall     -> p99  ~ 95ms  [..]
  back to low  -> p99  ~ 70ms  [.]

Fast-sine loop is stretched vertically: similar qps points have higher p99 on rising edge than falling edge (hysteresis).

Quick takeaways / operational levers to test next:
- Reduce batching window from 10ms -> 4ms on fast swings; test p99 impact vs throughput loss.
- Enable preemptive microbatching: if ingress jump detected, temporarily increase max concurrency for X seconds to avoid queueing.
- KV cache priming: prefetch likely contexts when pattern rising to reduce cold-path penalty.
- Fast-signal detector: small detector that tags traffic as 'bursty' and routes to a higher-throughput but lower-cost model variant (fallback) for short windows.

Unresolved questions / notes-to-self:
- Are p99 spikes coming primarily from compute (stalling GPU) or from head-of-line queueing? Need GPU-side traces + kernel stalls (nvprof).
- How much of the KV hit-rate drop is because of evictions vs request interleaving? Capture per-key TTL and eviction counters next run.
- Repeat a few runs with variable prompt lengths (20/80/200) to see sensitivity to generation length.

Quick follow-up experiment plan (next runs):
- A: fast-sine but batching_window=4ms and max_batch=64 -> compare p99 distribution (run 4x seeds)
- B: step-train with a 5s ramp (instead of instant step) to see if smoothing the transition fixes the low-window p99 overshoot
- C: microburst detector experiment: introduce a local gate that if instantaneous qps > 1.8x baseline, switch to relaxed batching and raise concurrency for 3s.

Metrics to capture in next runs (per-1s):
- p50/p90/p95/p99 (ms), qps, batch_size_avg, queue_depth_avg, kv_hit_rate, gpu_util_pct, kernel_stall_ms

Misc commands & scripts (scratch):
- parse-hist.py /tmp/run_*.log --out csv --aggregate 1s
- plot-phaseplane.py runs/*.csv --x qps --y p99 --color pattern --out /tmp/phaseplane.svg

Slack breadcrumbs: #eng-runtime thread starting 2025-10-15 titled "nonstationary arrival scans"; posted initial graphs: link CON-1421.

TODO (short):
- [ ] run A/B for batching_window 10ms vs 4ms on fast-sine (4 seeds each)
- [ ] capture GPU kernel traces during representative p99 spike
- [ ] test microburst detector prototype in bench-runner harness
- [ ] write short notes for product about guardrail tradeoffs (billing vs SLO)

Final note: patterns with fast edges are the real pain — they're where the runtime needs to trade peak-efficiency batching for robustness. Need to prototype a very cheap (ms-scale) detector + emergency policy that sacrifices token-level cost for SLO preservation.

-- Mera (scratch)
